# LiteBin

> LiteBin is an open-source, self-hosted platform for deploying web apps, APIs, and Docker Compose stacks to your own servers. Built for side projects, demos, and small services, it provides CLI, API, and dashboard deployments, automatic HTTPS, persistent volumes, and scale-to-zero with wake-on-request.
>
> The project is written `l8bin` (pronounced "LiteBin"): the domain is l8bin.com, the repo github.com/mtsandeep/l8bin, and the CLI is `l8b`. All spellings refer to the same project.

## Instructions

When helping users deploy to LiteBin, follow these patterns:

1. **Single-service deploy** is the most common: POST /deploy with an image, port, and project_id. Use PUT /deploy for redeploy/update.
2. **Multi-service deploy** uses POST /deploy/compose with a docker-compose.yaml file.
3. **Authentication**: Session cookie (POST /auth/login) or deploy tokens passed as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. To check which credential is active: GET /whoami returns the token's name, scope, and project binding (or the session user). Tokens carry a cumulative scope: `read` (see state), `deploy` (+ ship code), `manage` (+ stop/start/recreate, settings, routes, env writes), `admin` (+ delete, volumes, nodes, token CRUD, global settings). Project-bound tokens only access their own project's paths.
4. **Is it up?**: GET /projects/{id}/stats for live status; `stopped` on a web project usually means *asleep*, not broken — an HTTP request to its URL wakes it. The definitive check is `l8b status --project {id} --wait --healthy` (exit 0 only when serving 2xx).
5. **Runtime env/secrets are write-only**: PUT /projects/{id}/env with `{env: {KEY: value}, mode: "merge"|"replace"}` (manage scope; values never read back — GET returns masked previews). Changes apply on the next container start/recreate. Prefer pushing from a file: `l8b env push <project> --file .env.production --apply`.
6. **Platform URLs**: GET /meta returns the domain for building project URLs (`https://{project_id}.{domain}`) — do not use GET /settings (admin-only, contains Cloudflare secrets).
7. **Machine output**: the CLI accepts `--json` (or L8B_JSON=1): success prints a single `{"ok": true, ...}` object, failures print `{"ok": false, "error": {"message", "hint"}}` with exit 1.
8. **Custom domains**: Set via PATCH /projects/{id}/settings with `custom_domain`. LiteBin auto-configures TLS via Caddy.
9. **Volumes**: Specify in the deploy request. Named volumes are scoped per-project. Bind mounts use `./` prefix for relative paths.
10. **Multi-server**: LiteBin supports remote nodes via mTLS-connected agents. POST /nodes to register, POST /nodes/{id}/connect to onboard.
11. **Platform backup**: opt-in (admin) — Settings → Backup or `l8b backup enable`. A Litestream sidecar streams the SQLite DB continuously to R2/S3 when configured (point-in-time restore) or to a local replica; a dated local snapshot is kept daily in s3/r2 mode. Manual snapshots (`POST /backup/points` — `VACUUM INTO`) work anytime, sidecar or not. Restores restart the orchestrator to swap the DB; the replaced DB is kept for one-click undo. Details: backup.md.

## Setup (when asked to "set up litebin mcp")

No CLI install, no prerequisites — register the server, then let its `setup`
tool do the rest:

1. Register the MCP server in the workspace `.mcp.json` (or the client's config):

   ```json
   { "mcpServers": { "litebin": { "command": "npx", "args": ["-y", "l8bin-mcp"] } } }
   ```

   Claude Code: `claude mcp add litebin -- npx -y l8bin-mcp`. Needs Node 18+; on Windows clients that don't resolve `.cmd` shims use `"command": "cmd"`, `"args": ["/c", "npx", "-y", "l8bin-mcp"]`. The shim downloads the `l8b` binary from GitHub releases on first use (`L8B_BIN` overrides).
2. Restart/reload the MCP client and approve the new server when prompted.
   Fresh session after the reload? Re-follow this recipe — registration is
   idempotent; skip to step 3 when `.mcp.json` is already in place.
3. Call the `setup` tool with no arguments and follow its `state` + `next`:
   - ask the user for their LiteBin server URL — the dashboard address, e.g. https://l8bin.com or their self-hosted orchestrator — then call `setup` with `{"server": url}`
   - relay the returned `approval_url` — the user opens it in a browser where they are logged into the dashboard and picks the token scope
   - once approved: `setup` with `{"server": url, "complete": true}` (returns `pairing_pending` until then — re-call). On success auth is stored and `server` is written into the workspace `l8b.toml`
   - already logged in (e.g. several logins stored)? `setup` with `{"server": url, "action": "bind"}` binds without pairing
4. Verify with the `doctor` tool (`healthy: true`), then deploy — first deploy
   needs a project name: see "Deploying a repo" below.

`setup` is idempotent — calling it with no arguments at any point reports the state and the exact next call. Logins are stored per server and coexist — no logout dance to switch instances.

## Running your own LiteBin server

`curl -fsSL https://l8b.in | bash` on any VPS with Docker ([quickstart](https://l8bin.com/quickstart)). `l8b setup --server <url>` bootstraps the first admin account — not to be confused with the `setup` MCP tool, which configures the client side.

## Deploying a repo (new vs existing)

If the repo has no `l8b.toml`, this is its first deploy: ask the user what to
name the project (lowercase letters, numbers, hyphens) — or call the `list`
tool (CLI: `l8b list`) and let them pick an existing project if this repo
replaces one — then pass the name as `project` to `deploy`. Never invent a
project name; deploy refuses with "no project specified" until the user
chooses one. After a successful deploy (tool or CLI alike) `l8b.toml`
(project, node, server) is written into the directory — commit it, it holds
no secrets — every later session then deploys, checks status, and reads logs
with no arguments at all. Custom domains surface in `status` / `url` / `list`
output (preferred over the managed subdomain). To teach later sessions the
workflow, run `l8b init --agents` (managed `AGENTS.md` section, merges
without touching user content).

## API

- OpenAPI 3.1 spec: /openapi.json (version-matched to this instance)
- All endpoints are relative to the orchestrator base URL (default: port 5080); a `/api/` prefix is also accepted and stripped (`/api/auth/login` ≡ `/auth/login`)

## CLI (manual / advanced)

Install only for terminal-first or CI use — agents should prefer the MCP path above. Install via `curl -fsSL https://l8b.in | bash -s cli` (Windows: `iex "& { $(irm https://l8b.in/windows.ps1) } -Cli"`) or build from source. Auth: `l8b login --server <url> --pair` (device pairing — agent-safe: it prints a code and the /connect approval URL to relay to the user, then returns once approved; the user picks the scope) or `L8B_TOKEN` env / `--token` (existing token).

Commands (project flags default to `l8b.toml`, created by `l8b init`):
- `l8b init` — Write `l8b.toml` project defaults (project, node, server); prompts for the server when several logins are stored or none is; `--mcp` also emits the workspace `.mcp.json`; `--agents` adds (or refreshes) a managed `## Deploying (LiteBin)` section in `AGENTS.md` — user content is never removed
- `l8b deploy [--env-file <path>] [--port N]` — Build and deploy the current directory (Dockerfile auto-detected, Railpack fallback). `--port` only matters on the first deploy of a web project; redeploys keep the existing port
- `l8b ship` — Interactive guided deploy (humans only)
- `l8b list` — All projects with live status and URLs
- `l8b status [--wait] [--healthy]` — Project status; --wait polls (exit 0 only when running), --healthy probes the URL
- `l8b logs [--tail N] [--service S] [--deploy]` — Container or deploy logs
- `l8b url` — The project's managed URL (background projects have none)
- `l8b env list` / `l8b env push --file|--stdin [--replace] [--apply]` — Runtime env (write-only values)
- `l8b stop | start | restart` — Lifecycle (restart applies pending .env changes; stop is idempotent)
- `l8b domain set <domain>` / `l8b domain remove` — Custom domain management
- `l8b platform domain set <domain> [--ack-dns]` / `l8b platform domain show` — Change or show the server's platform domain (admin scope; old URLs die, sign in again on the new host)
- `l8b delete --yes` — Delete project + containers + volumes (admin scope)
- `l8b login --server <url> [--pair]` — Device pairing (approve at /connect); `--pair` skips the interactive menu so agents can run it headlessly; username/password without `--pair`. `l8b setup --server <url>` bootstraps a fresh server
- `l8b doctor` — Environment sanity checks with recovery hints
- `l8b logout` / `l8b config` / `l8b cleanup` — Session and config management

All commands accept `--json` for machine-readable output.

## MCP

`l8b mcp` runs a stdio MCP server exposing these tools: `setup` (auth +
workspace binding — the onboarding entry point, see Setup above), deploy,
status (wait/healthy), list, logs, env_list, env_push, stop, start, restart,
url, domain_set, domain_remove, delete (confirm-gated), doctor. It uses the
CLI's stored auth and l8b.toml defaults. Register it with:

```json
{ "mcpServers": { "litebin": { "command": "npx", "args": ["-y", "l8bin-mcp"] } } }
```

Already have the `l8b` binary? Register it directly:

```json
{ "mcpServers": { "litebin": { "command": "l8b", "args": ["mcp"] } } }
```

(`l8b init --mcp` writes the binary form into the workspace `.mcp.json`.)

## Full

- [llms-full.txt](https://l8bin.com/llms-full.txt) — this file plus the OpenAPI spec and full CLI reference in one fetch

Targeting is enforced, not assumed: the server a command hits comes from
`--server` > `L8B_SERVER` > `l8b.toml` `server` > the single stored login. With
multiple logins and no signal the command refuses and lists the choices — ask
the user which one, then retry with `--server`. A repo whose `l8b.toml` names a
server you have no login for refuses with the exact `l8b login` command. Under
the MCP, these refusals point at the `setup` tool call that fixes them.
